items.title: Stuart Bergen Interview, 1970-07-18
items.q: I loaned Mr. Gobert's wife my chord book. And she studied piano. And she punched the chords.

ctx.x: What about the Optimist Jazzers? That's a thing I forgot to ask about. That was a civic deal where the union let us play with the Optimist Club.

Bill Craze got me into that. Bill was a fine trombone player. And we had three amateurs and three pros. We had Bill Craze on the trombone, myself on the trumpet, Francis Murray, and I told you he was a fine tenor man. He played tenor and clarinet. Well that was really my front line. Every time we played with them we got some practice. I loaned Mr. Gobert's wife my chord book. And she studied piano. And she punched the chords. And Mr. Gobert, he played the Hoot Nanny. I played some washtub with a broomstick on it,…
The C melody was at all popular when you were coming up?
